description: Temporary security debt accepted so the guardrail can block new regressions while existing Tauri filesystem permissions are narrowed incrementally. Tauri application-data aliases are identifier-scoped. Dedicated release and Actions-maintenance workflows have reviewed write requirements.

acceptedFindings.reason: Legacy Tauri file bridge still relies on the broad fs plugin default. Replace with explicit fs permissions and backend-validated vault writes.
Tauri resolves $APPDATA to Elephant's identifier-scoped application data directory. The renderer bootstrap and settings persistence require access to that application-owned directory.
Legacy vault selection can currently target user home files. Replace with user-selected vault roots mediated by Rust validation.
Legacy vault selection can currently target Documents. Replace with scoped vault grants.
Legacy vault selection can currently target Downloads. Replace with scoped vault grants.
Legacy vault selection can currently target Desktop. Replace with scoped vault grants.
Temporary local LLM/runtime bridge debt. Replace wildcard localhost CSP with exact runtime ports before hardening production builds.
Temporary local LLM/runtime bridge debt. Replace wildcard localhost CSP with exact runtime ports before hardening production builds.
Legacy renderer bridge still expects the global Tauri API. Migrate callers to explicit @tauri-apps/api imports before disabling it.
Dedicated tag-triggered release workflow: it publishes the exact tagged ElephantNote application artifacts to the GitHub release and has no pull_request trigger.

Dedicated release workflow: it publishes signed and hashed platform-specific .enaddon archives to feature/physical-addon-catalog. It has no pull_request trigger and needs branch write access only for the final catalogue publication job.

Dedicated storage-maintenance workflow: it has no pull_request trigger, keeps contents read-only, and needs Actions write access only to delete repository artifacts and explicitly requested caches through GitHub's Actions API.
